NEW ANGLES, none decisive: (1) Internet Archive full-text search of the crag guidebook (Weekend Rock Washington) for the beta-box structure: its beta boxes carry Drive time / Getting there / Concessions lines and no fee or pass field; the only pass statements found in the book are the introduction (some areas require the Northwest Forest Pass, a good number are still free) and Washington Pass (pass mandated at the Blue Lake trailhead). Queries pairing Half Moon with fees, Forest Pass, Forest Service, parking, pull off, hairpin, 1.4 miles, season, services returned no Half Moon fragment speaking to a pass. Absence in fragments, not counted. (2) Mountain Project Treasury bouldering (parks on the same road, on the left just before the third switchback): no pass, fee or permit text. (3) A third-party Iron Goat Trail guide (irongoat.org) speaks only of the Iron Goat trailheads (pass needed there), not this pull-off. (4) Search results for Old Cascade Highway / Old Stevens Pass Highway pass statements again return only the Iron Goat / Wellington / Martin Creek trailheads and a new MP 58 Iron Goat trailhead on US 2 (no pass there), none of them this pull-off. (5) CascadeClimbers: still only the Seattle gym of that name. (6) Discover Pass does not apply: the road is a national forest road (FS 6099), not state land — reasoning, not a source. Net: unchanged; two-source rule not met. Owner note unchanged: the row contradicts itself; if the owner accepts land manager + row, the op is access.passRequired "Recreation pass" -> a scoped no-pass value (e.g. "None — the pull-off is not a fee site") on these five rows only; access.fees and access._raw untouched.

results.summary: Day 1 (6.2 mi to Cooney Lake on the Foggy Dew / Merchants Basin line) still has only one stated trailhead-to-lake figure (8.5), so no change; day 2 left alone.
results.evidence: Sixth pass (r16, 2026-10-01). Row re-read read-only: itinerary days[0].miles 6.2, days[1].miles 12.8, days[1].note restates "the full 6.2 miles back out"; Cooney Lake pin distMi 8. NEW ANGLES via Internet Archive full-text search across every scanned book naming Cooney Lake with Merchants Basin / Foggy Dew (22 books), plus web: (1) Mountain Biking the Methow Valley (Barnett, 2001), Foggy Dew—Merchant Basin and Cooney Lake, 16.0 mi: its log goes up #417, takes the trail 429 (Martin Creek) junction to Cooney Lake and only then tops out on a saddle overlooking Merchant Basin at 9.5 — the reverse loop via Martin Creek, not the row line, and no Cooney Lake figure surfaced in the fragments. (2) Mountain Biking Washington (Poffenbarger) repeats the 8.5 Cooney Lake Campground figure verbatim from Mountain Bike America: Washington — same author, ONE source (not a second). (3) Hiking the Great Northwest (Manning/Spring, 1991): Cooney Lake 9 mi from the road via Eagle Lakes trail and Martin Creek trail No. 429 — Crater Creek start, not this line. (4) Pacific Northwest Hiking (Judd & Nelson, 1995/1997/2002): Cooney Lake entry reaches the lake about five miles from its trailhead on the Martin Creek side and joins the Foggy Dew trail below Merchants Basin — not this line. (5) Mountain Biking Washington (Black, 1999) and Mountain Bike! Washington (Bennett): Cooney Lake rides start at the Crater Creek trailhead. (6) Backpacking Washington (Lorain): Day 1 Cooney Lake 8.8 on a multi-day Sawtooth trip whose start is not this line in the fragments. (7) Cascade Alpine Guide (Beckey): Foggy Dew Creek Trail to the Summit Trail in 8.4 mi via Merchants Basin and Switchback Pass — a different endpoint. (8) New WTA trip reports: 2018-07-30 (junction for Merchants Basin or Cooney Lake at about 6 miles, no lake figure); 2020-09-01 (junction at five miles; a Summit Trail sign about a mile past the Cooney Lake spur reads 8 miles to Foggy Dew Creek — a sign beyond the lake on the ridge, not a trailhead-to-lake figure). (9) USFS Foggy Dew Trailhead page and Sawtooth Backcountry brochure: segments only (#417 5.0, #434 1.5). (10) Trailforks Foggy Lollipop route: 403, no Wayback copy. Net: still one stated figure on the row line (Mountain Bike America / Mountain Biking Washington, 8.5, one author). No op on days[0].miles, days[1].note or days[1].miles. Owner note unchanged: 8.5 (single source) and the row own Cooney Lake pin (distMi 8) both contradict 6.2; the day-1 note wording (turn off onto the Cooney Lake trail at the Merchants Basin junction) can also be read as the 5-mile Martin Creek junction, where the published one-way figures still disagree (7.0 / 7.6-7.8 / 7.7 to the junction).
